clue.text: Cat turned against me in confused situation

indicators.note: something turned faces the other way, so this word is read from its end back to its start

blocks.note: taken as written
puss is an informal word for a cat

explanation.surface: A cat rounds on its owner amid general chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' just places the two parts side by side, the pronoun first.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess-up is a botched, muddled state of affairs, so it is a confused situation.

clue.text: Graduate in chaotic system lacking time for mission

indicators.note: lacking means without, and time is abbreviated to one letter, so that letter is dropped
something chaotic is in disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled
in places the degree abbreviation inside the jumbled letters

blocks.note: taken as written before losing a letter
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate caught up in a disorganised system, with no time left for the mission.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic mission is the staff or building representing one country in another.

clue.text: Part of process is altering fibre

indicators.note: the answer is only a part of the following words, sitting within them

blocks.note: found across the end of process, is, and the start of altering

explanation.surface: Part of the manufacturing method involves changing a textile.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff natural fibre from an agave plant, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Most important pair, batting around middle of innings, supported by friend

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter, so only that one is kept
in a down clue what is supported sits on top, so the friend comes underneath, at the end

blocks.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair
a cricket side batting is in
C stands for circa, Latin for around
the fourth of seven letters
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary: the key pair at the crease mid-innings, backed up by a teammate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like it wraps something, but it is C for circa, one piece in a straight run.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal as an adjective means chief or foremost, first in rank or importance.

clue.text: Our lot, retreating, long offering no resistance

indicators.note: a retreating force goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: our lot is us
to long for something is to pine for it

explanation.surface: Our troops fall back, having long since given up fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means passive or inert, failing to act or object, hence putting up no resistance.

clue.text: Sign of agreement after second year in council

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
Y is the abbreviation for year
a nod signals agreement

explanation.surface: A motion is nodded through at a council meeting after a second year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the sign of agreement behind the two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of church clergy and officials, a governing ecclesiastical council.

clue.text: Abundant input fell disastrously

indicators.note: something that went disastrously fell apart, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A large amount of input dropped off badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something existing in large quantities, more than enough.

clue.text: Sport to be announced in ring, first off

indicators.note: with the first off, the opening letter is removed from the word
in places the abbreviation inside the shortened word

blocks.note: a knell is the ring of a bell
TBA is the usual abbreviation for to be announced

explanation.surface: A sport whose details are yet to be revealed within the boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' is a bell's toll, not a boxing ring; without its K it becomes NELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team game, popular in Britain and the Commonwealth, where players shoot a ball into a high ring.

clue.text: Event, initially unprofitable ball, involving outfit with unknown song

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept
involving means taking in, so the outfit goes inside the ball

blocks.note: the first letter of event
a lean year is an unprofitable one
an orb is a ball or sphere
a rig is an outfit of clothing
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An evening where a loss-making dance involves dressing up and a mystery song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' looks like a dance in the surface, but it is a sphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor Rigby is a 1966 Beatles song about lonely people, from the album Revolver.

clue.text: A vital test's been arranged for racing driver

indicators.note: things that have been arranged are put into a new order, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A crucial trial has been set up for a motor-racing driver.
explanation.walkthrough: Sebastian Vettel is the German driver who won four Formula One world championships.
explanation.definitionFit: Vettel won four Formula One world titles with Red Bull, so he is a famous example of a racing driver.

clue.text: Working on usual items at the same time

indicators.note: working means being worked into a new shape, so these letters are reformed

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Multitasking: dealing with ordinary jobs all at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Simultaneous describes events that occur together, happening concurrently in the same moment.

clue.text: Is power held by quiet, retiring editor given to wrong person?

indicators.note: what is held by something sits inside its grasp, so these letters go within the other word
retiring means withdrawing or going backwards, so the word for quiet is read in reverse

blocks.note: calm means quiet, still
taken as written
P is the symbol for power in physics
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A retiring editor wonders whether influence has been handed to the wrong person.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'quiet' and 'retiring' describe the editor in the surface, but 'retiring' turns the word for quiet round, and the editor's abbreviation comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Misplaced trust or affection is bestowed on someone who does not deserve it, hence given to the wrong person.

clue.text: Crown obtained by one occupying seat of ancient kings

indicators.note: someone occupying a place sits inside it, so this letter goes within the other word

blocks.note: the Hill of Tara in Ireland was the seat of the ancient High Kings
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A crown won by whoever sits on the throne of the old kings.
explanation.walkthrough: Tara, in County Meath, Ireland, is where the High Kings of Ireland were traditionally inaugurated.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head, a kind of small crown.

clue.text: Large old university, not English? True

indicators.note: not means leave out, and English is abbreviated as one letter, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
O is a standard abbreviation for old
Yale is a well-known American university

explanation.surface: A large, long-established university that is not in England: a real one.
explanation.definitionFit: True in the sense of faithful or steadfast in allegiance, as in a true friend.

clue.text: Innkeepers in line as well as noblemen

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
and means as well as
lords are noblemen

explanation.surface: Pub owners queue up beside members of the aristocracy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a pub landlord is the person who runs the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Landlords who run pubs or inns serve drinks and keep the house, much like innkeepers.

clue.text: Left fine miscellany in collection of representative works

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship
F stands for fine on pencil grades
an olio is a mixture or miscellany

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a good assortment in a collection of works.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or designer's portfolio is a set of samples showing the range of their work.

clue.text: Tormented about area, north and south, being plundered

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for tormented goes round the other letters

blocks.note: racked means tormented, tortured
A is the abbreviation for area
N is the abbreviation for north
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A region suffers torment from end to end as it is looted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north and south' look like a sweep from top to bottom, but they are just two compass abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Ransacked describes a place gone through and stripped of valuables, so it is being robbed or looted.

clue.text: What raises blood pressure? Democrat in realm reversing nothing

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for the party member inside the word for realm
reversing means going backwards, so the word for nothing is written back to front

blocks.note: an arena is a sphere or realm of activity
D is the abbreviation for Democrat
nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A political question about what gets a Democrat's blood pressure up.
explanation.definitionFit: The adrenal hormone prepares the body for fight or flight, increasing heart rate and blood pressure.

clue.text: Live screening beginning to upset balance

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind or around, so the letter goes inside the word for live
the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is all that is used

blocks.note: to live somewhere is to reside there
the first letter of upset

explanation.surface: A live broadcast threatens to tip the balance.
explanation.definitionFit: Residue is what remains after the rest is used up, just as a balance is the remainder.

clue.text: Failure in variety of roles

indicators.note: a variety offers different versions, so the letters of the word appear in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor who flops in a range of parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is a person who habitually fails, so the word names a failure.

clue.text: Adhesive label with small heart

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
ticker is slang for the heart

explanation.surface: A label with a little heart drawn on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticker is a printed piece of paper or plastic backed with glue for attaching to things.

clue.text: Comfort leader in last stand

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: to comfort is to ease
the opening letter of last

explanation.surface: A leader takes solace in making one final stand.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a wooden frame that holds a painter's canvas or a display board upright.

clue.text: Male swan, bereft of company, wandering bird

indicators.note: bereft means deprived, and company is shortened to two letters, so those are removed

blocks.note: a cob is a male swan
rambling means wandering about

explanation.surface: A lone cob swan drifts about, cut off from its group.
explanation.walkthrough: CO is the usual abbreviation for company; taking it from COB leaves B.
explanation.definitionFit: The brambling is a finch that visits Britain in winter, so it is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Toast knight after summit

blocks.note: the brow of a hill is its top
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Drinking a toast to a knight after reaching the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' suggests raising a glass, but here it is a verb for cooking. 'after' puts the knight at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast bread is to grill it until it colours, which is to brown it.

clue.text: Extra payment in end for job with responsibility

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of job
an onus is a duty or responsibility

explanation.surface: A worker given extra pay at the close of a job that carries responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is money paid on top of normal wages, often as a reward for performance.

clue.text: Imprisoned in dark den, lucky one getting free

indicators.note: letters getting free break loose from their order and can be reassembled differently

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A captive in a dark den is the fortunate one who escapes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something locked securely away, so a person held that way is jailed.

clue.text: Class? There's not so much about

blocks.note: less means not so much
on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Is there a smaller class going around?
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson is a period of teaching at school, also called a class.

clue.text: Leave area without vegetation

blocks.note: first meaning: to abandon, a verb
second meaning: a barren, arid region, a noun

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: stress on the second syllable for the verb, the first for the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon a post is to run away from duty, and the noun names an arid, barren stretch of land.
